# [BUG] Frontend CI failing: service tests broken by async backend-resolution health probe

## Bug
Frontend CI (`Frontend CI` workflow) has been failing on `develop` since commit 8ed067c (#151) — 5+ consecutive runs red, e.g. run 31478764130. `npm run test` fails in `src/services/TMDB.test.js`, `user.test.js`, and `media.test.js` with assertions like "expected undefined to be '...auth/register'" and URLs resolving to `/actuator/health` instead of the real endpoint.

## Root Cause
#151 replaced `getApiUrl()`'s synchronous hostname check with an async, health-checked waterfall (`resolveApiUrl()` in `apiUrl.js`) that issues a real `fetch(...)` health probe to `/actuator/health` before returning a backend URL. These three test files never set a static override, so under jsdom's default `localhost` hostname they fall into that waterfall — the health-probe fetch call lands at `mock.calls[0]`, which is what each test's `fetchedRequest()`/`fetchedUrl()` helper reads as "the actual request." `apiUrl.test.js` already covers the waterfall itself correctly; the bug is only in these three consumers still assuming the old synchronous contract (one even has a comment describing the old behavior).

## Severity vs. Priority
**Severity (technical impact):** Major — blocks CI on every frontend push, but doesn't affect the running app.
**Priority (business urgency):** P1

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Fixed and verified live — `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (200/200 passing), `npm run test:coverage` (89.9% stmts, above the 80% gate), and `npm run build` all pass locally against the fix.
- [x] Regression test added — the three fixed test files now pin `filmpire_api_url` via `localStorage` before dispatch, which both fixes and correctly regression-tests the static-override short-circuit contract that `createDynamicBaseQuery` relies on.

## Notes
Fix pins a static `filmpire_api_url` override in each test's setup instead of touching `apiUrl.js` — the async waterfall itself is intentional and already has dedicated coverage in `apiUrl.test.js`.
